ceo_anna: Quick follow-up from todays all-hands Q&A on strategy. Wanted to pull a few specific clarifying questions into this thread so teams have clear direction. Please keep replies short so we can action.

pm_jordan: Thanks Anna. Question 1: within 'predictable economics' are we aiming to lead on price, latency, both, or position as best tradeoff?

cto_lee: Short answer: tradeoff. We shouldn't beat hyperscalers on raw lowest price for generic models, but we should own the price vs latency sweet spot for production workloads (tail latency + effective cost). Practically: publish benchmarks that show lower cost-to-serve at p95/p99 compared to self-hosted variants across common workloads.

product_nia: For messaging: do we call out specific competitor categories (hyperscalers vs OSS runtimes) or keep it higher level?

ceo_anna: Call out categories. Customers ask: hyperscalers, specialized inference vendors, and OSS stacks. We need clear copy that explains how Redwood differs in three dimensions: deployment flexibility, operational guarantees, and cost predictability.

eng_lead_maya: What's the ask for eng teams re: benchmarks? We can produce a 'redwood-standard' benchmark harness but need scope.

research_asha: Suggestion: start with three workloads: short-chat (<=128), high-throughput embeddings, and long-context summarization. For each measure: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec cost, and failure/retry rates under 2x load. That gives a broad picture.

sales_sam: From field: prospects ask about migration friction. Can we provide a clear migration story (config export, compatible model variants, data path)? Should be short and concrete.

ops_rita: Also add compliance & auditing checklist for customers to compare vs on-prem. We should have a slide with one-line answers: encryption, audit logs, SLAs, data residency.

pm_jordan: Actionable items I captured: 1) @eng_lead_maya + @research_asha define benchmark harness and target workloads (due Tue) 2) @product_nia + @sales_sam draft migration one-pager (due Thu) 3) @ops_rita assemble compliance checklist (due Fri) 4) @cto_lee publish a short statement on defense (why our runtime matters) for the RFP kit (due Mon).

product_nia: For the migration one-pager Ill include a small snippet customers can copy into their architecture doc: ``
- export model config (yaml)
- convert weights (if needed) with redwood-convert
- deploy to dedicated/private with env vars preserved
``
Would that help?

cto_lee: Yes. Keep it pragmatic. Include common gotchas (KV cache priming, prompt length defaults, and batching configs).

ceo_anna: One more ask: competitive listening. @sales_sam and @research_asha coordinate a shared doc with three bullet takeaway per competitor (strength, weakness, likely ask). Keep it short.

allhands_bot: Slides & recording uploaded: https://redwood.internal/all-hands/1954998765 (note: public links will follow).

pm_jordan: Thanks all. I'll synthesize the inputs into a 1-page strategy memo and post by Monday AM. Quick thumbs if you agree with the plan.
